Detroit is 3-0 with an adjusted net of +5.7 per 100, but that is shrunk heavily from three games. The raw eFG of 0.563 is probably above what they will sustain.
New York is 0-3 with a raw offense of 101.7 points per game and eFG of 0.476. The adjusted net is still +1.1, so the ratings treat the slow start as partly noise.
Jalen Duren is out and his absence is already in the projection (+2.0 margin, -1.2 total, DET missing 5.5 points of value). I add nothing on top.
Both defenses are strong against centers: NYK allows -10% points and DET allows -15%. Neither team's interior scoring should get much easier, which supports a total near the market.
risks: Ausar Thompson (ankle, day-to-day, full participant at shootaround) and Isaiah Joe (hip, questionable) could change Detroit's rotation late.
A three-game sample means both teams' ratings could move a lot. A 0-3 Knicks team at home could also rebound toward its adjusted level.
Detroit takes 43% of its shots from three and NYK allows 46% (league 42%), so shooting variance could swing the total either way.
matchups: Detroit's rim-heavy shot mix (37% at the rim) faces a Knicks defense that allows 30% at the rim, which is average. Without Duren, Detroit has less size to finish there (from memory).
